derivation: bith 'hot' + S lern 'the face' + -en ('of, belonging to') (compound: the head softened, §3.10): the adjective of bithlern O0099, made as bridlernen O0156 and rerddhalden O2074 are; unit S08 (V.5, 'the south gun')
desir 'late, after the time' + -el ('-ish': quality + -el, as dommel O0475, sulvel O2433); unit S08 (V.5, 'they came a little late')

meanings: the root-men: their plain name ('the men of the root'); the wall's own diminutive for them is meskel O1385, 'treelings'
derivation: a phrase: uldath man-PL (uld + -Ath) + veskrivull S·root (meskrivull O1389, m > v: the possessor softened in the construct, as Molt Veskrivull O1419); unit S08 (V.5: 'the root-men … the wall calls them treelings', where the two must differ)

meanings: the Fall (of the Shorelands): 'the falling'; et Ommol
derivation: omm 'fall' + -Ol (verbal noun), the event's name (as Vess Vollol O2738); the common noun is ommol O1869; unit S08 (V.5: 'names for them from the Fall')

meanings: the stone leaf: a leaf of the Rivenmen's telling ('the leaf of the stone')

meanings: the wood's leaf: the facing leaf, the Mystwood's knowing ('the leaf of the wood')
derivation: a phrase: flenn leaf + et the + mesk wood (the construct); unit S08 (V.5)

orrowen: doss flenn et mesk ul o lern
meanings: the wood's leaf faces it (the close of a stone leaf's headnote: 'the leaf of the wood is in its face')
derivation: a phrase: doss be + flenn et mesk the wood's leaf + ul lern in the face of O2631, with the pronoun possessor o between them (as ul o rask, pilot IV.4; and IV.4's doss o ul lern Yebb et Pard, 'it faces the Warden's Door'); unit S08 (V.5), the same words as S05 (III.1)

meanings: two by two, in pairs ('two and two')
derivation: a phrase: pa two (+S) + eth and + pa two, as hos eth hos O2862 'one by one'; unit S08 (V.5: 'they came in pairs now')

meanings: a breath apart ('one breath in the mortar between'): of things that come one after another
derivation: a phrase: hos one + hoss breath + ul lodh between O2628/O1221 ('in the mortar of'); unit S08 (V.5: 'one sail went pale, and then the next … a breath apart')

meanings: in order, in line ('in course'): of a line of men or of hulls, as of a course of stones
derivation: a phrase: ul in (+N) + drenn N·course (trenn O2579), as ul drenn vodh O2864 'in what order'; unit S08 (V.5: 'some did not come on in order at all')

meanings: it means it, it is in earnest ('it is true'): of a hull that leans to the shore

meanings: The fleet has spent its fire (the wall's saying at noon: 'the fire of the fleet is spent')
derivation: a phrase: doss be + vorr fire + et scethan the fleet (the construct) + vyssorat spent O2806 (vyssor + -At); unit S08 (V.5)

orrowen: Naelur et molt sa luskith lont
meanings: Choose which heart you leave them (the wall's saying at the fire: 'choose the heart that you leave at them')
derivation: a phrase: naelur choose (IMP) + et molt the heart + sa REL (+S) + luskith S·leave-2SG (lusk: l unchanged) + lont at-3PL; unit S08 (V.5)

meanings: keep its courses: keep its spacing, keep formation (of a feigned rout, as a wall keeps its courses)
derivation: a phrase: keth hold, keep + o its (+S) + dhrenneth S·courses (trenneth O2586, t > dh: the softening shows the possessive, §3.5); unit S08 (V.5: 'a feigned one keeps its spacing')

meanings: is (it)? is (it) still?: the yes-or-no question of the state verb doss
